zh: 『何书办说，这件事一进一出，关系极大，如果袁老爷的中书还不出娘家，不但升同知不必谈，还要追究他何以资历不符，那就不是吏部的事了。』『不是吏部的事，』徐世昌问∶『是哪一部的事呢？』『刑部。』『好家伙！』徐世昌大吃一惊，『还要治罪啊！』『人家是这么说，咱们也不能全听他的。不过，袁老爷正好有这个短处非求他不可，那就只好听他狮子大开口了。』『要多少？』『两千。』正好差了一半；徐世昌面有难色，将袁世凯的信，递给了张瑞荫看。看完信，张瑞荫问道∶『老牛，他跟你说了没有，是怎么个办法？』『大少爷，你倒想，他肯跟我说吗？我倒是盯着问了好半天，他只跟我说了一句话∶「事不难办，不过就告诉了你，你也办不到。』『好吧，跟他讲盘子吧，最多给他一个半数。』张瑞荫又说∶『徐老爷的朋友，不是外人。』这时是暗示老牛别从中乱戴帽子∶『是！既然大少爷交代，我尽力去办就是。』老牛又说∶『我得连夜跟何书办去谈，不然人家天一亮就走人了。』
en: “Clerk He says the movements into and out of office make this a serious matter. If Mr Yuan’s secretaryship cannot be traced to its proper origin, promotion to deputy prefect is out of the question. There will also be an investigation into the discrepancy in his record. Then it will no longer concern the Ministry of Personnel.” “Which ministry would it concern?” Xu asked. “Punishments.” “Good heavens!” Xu was alarmed. “He could be prosecuted?” “That is what they say. We need not believe every word, but Mr Yuan has this weakness and must ask their help. We can only listen to an extravagant demand.” “How much?” “Two thousand.” Exactly twice the available sum. Looking troubled, Xu handed Yuan’s letter to Zhang Ruiyin. After reading it, Zhang asked, “Old Niu, did he tell you how he means to do it?” “Would he tell me, Young Master? I pressed him for ages. All he would say was, ‘The matter is not difficult, but even if I told you, you could not do it.’” “Very well. Bargain with him. Fifteen hundred at the most. Mr Xu’s friend is not an outsider.” This hinted that Old Niu must not inflate the price for his own benefit. “Yes. With your instructions, Young Master, I shall do my utmost. But I must negotiate with him tonight. He leaves at first light.”

zh: 连夜折冲，以一千二百两银子成交；先交一半，等办妥了再交一半。徐世昌第二天到天津，去北洋公所将一千两银子领了出来，存在阜康福钱庄，先打了一张六百两的票子，交给张瑞荫。张瑞荫办事也很周到，将老牛唤了来说道∶『你最好把何书办约出来，大家当面锣、对面鼓说明白。怕的万一出了什么差错，徐老爷对袁老爷也有个交代。』『是。』老牛便去约好何书办，在一家饭馆见面。部中胥吏的身份甚低，尽管衣着比纨绔子弟还讲究，但见了张瑞荫称『大少爷』，对徐世昌叫『徐老爷』，站着说话，执礼甚恭。等把银票递了过去，何书办接到手中，摆在桌上，然后请个安说∶『跟大少爷、徐老爷回，事情呢？一举手之劳，不过要经十三道关口，一关过不去就不成。银票我暂时收着，也不会去兑，等事情办妥了再说。』『是的，你多费心。』张瑞荫问∶『徐老爷应该怎么回复袁老爷？』『请徐老爷告诉袁老爷，说当初捐中书的名字不假，只为将门之后，投效戎行，所以改名「世凯」。只要北洋这么咨复吏部，一准改名，袁老爷的同知就升定了。』这个诀窍说穿了不稀奇，但如果不是在吏部打通了关节，一改名字就可能会把整个前程断送掉，因为要刁难的话，随便找个理由就可以折磨个一年半载，及至一关通过，又有另一关，非把钱花够了数，不能领一张俗称为『部照「的任官』文凭『，而在更名未确定以前，不能分发，不能赴任，只有闲等，先就是一大损失。所以考试发榜，吏部铨选，如果姓名弄错，往往情甘委屈，将错就错，象袁世凯这样顺利的假』更名『，实在很少。
en: After negotiations that night, they settled at twelve hundred taels: half in advance and half when the business was complete. The next day Xu went to Tianjin, collected the thousand taels from the Beiyang Office, deposited them at Fukangfu Bank and first obtained a note for six hundred, which he handed to Zhang. Zhang was thorough. He summoned Old Niu. “You had better arrange a meeting with Clerk He, so that everyone can speak plainly face to face. If anything goes wrong, Mr Xu must have an account to give Mr Yuan.” “Yes.” Old Niu arranged for them to meet at a restaurant. Ministry clerks occupied a low social position. Though He dressed more elegantly than a rich young dandy, he addressed Zhang as “Young Master” and Xu as “Mr Xu”, standing while he spoke and observing every courtesy. When the banknote was handed over, he placed it on the table, bowed and said, “To explain to you both: the task itself is no more than lifting a hand, but it must pass thirteen gates. Failure at any one of them will stop it. I shall keep the note for now without cashing it until the work is done.” “Very well. Thank you for your trouble,” Zhang said. “How should Mr Xu reply to Mr Yuan?” “Tell him that the name under which the secretaryship was purchased was genuine. As a descendant of a military family, he subsequently volunteered for service and adopted the name Shikai. Let Beiyang send that explanation to Personnel. Once the change of name is approved, his promotion is assured.” The device was simple once explained. Without connections smoothed at the ministry, however, a change of name could destroy an entire career. If the clerks wished to obstruct it, any excuse could delay the matter for six months or a year. After one barrier was passed, another would arise. Until enough money had been spent, no appointment warrant—the document commonly called a ministry certificate—would be issued. While the change remained unresolved, the man could neither be assigned a post nor take one up. Waiting alone was a substantial loss. Consequently, when a name was wrong in examination results or Personnel’s appointments, many willingly endured it and continued under the error. A fraudulent “name change” as smooth as Yuan’s was rare indeed.

zh: 即令如此，公文往返，也得半年工夫。其时局势又已有变化，李鸿章的回任已经定局了——从张树声父子无意间得罪了张佩纶以后，李鸿章发觉张树声对北洋有『久假不归』之势，便利用时机，极力拉拢张佩纶，走李鸿藻的路子，搞出来一个与张树声各回本任的结果，但李鸿章母丧尚不满一年，而朝鲜的内乱已经平定，不必再动用武力，就没有『墨从军』而且『夺情』的理由，好在洋务上棘手之事甚多，以需要李鸿章与各国公使折冲的借口，将李鸿章留了下来，等待适当的时机再颁回任之谕。当李鸿章自合肥老家入京时，在上海住了好些日子，对左宗棠打算驱逐李鸿章势力出两江的情形，印象深刻。同时，对洋务、军务的见解，大相径庭，象中国与法国在越南的纠纷，李鸿章认为『彼欲难餍，我饷难支』，应该和平了结，决不可用武，而左宗棠主张支持助越拒法的『黑旗军「刘永福，不但以军火接济云贵总督岑毓英转以援刘，而且正式致书总理衙门，认为』主战主和，不难一言而决『，目前的情势，』不但泰西诸邦多以法为不然；逆料其与中国不协，必致事无结束，悔不可追『，就是法国亦何尝不顾虑，真要与中国开战，危险甚大，不过势成骑虎，不能不虚张声势，如果中国动摇，适中其计。他说他』默察时局，惟主战于正义有合，而于时势攸宜，即中外人情亦无不顺『就因为他一直有这种论调，所以朝廷特派李鸿章前赴广东督办越南事宜；这是一个名义，实际上李鸿章并不必赴广东，在上海、在天津，都可以跟法国公使宝海和谈。但如左宗棠不断鼓吹武力干预，到最后恐终不免要到广东去指挥对法战事，那一来只怕非身败名裂不可。当然，总署亦很持重，不会轻信左宗棠的『正义』说，只是李鸿章跟宝海的交涉，因此而愈感困难。
en: Even so, the exchange of official documents took half a year. By then the situation had changed again: Li Hongzhang’s return to his former post was settled. After Zhang Shusheng and his son inadvertently offended Zhang Peilun, Li realised that Zhang Shusheng seemed inclined to borrow Beiyang indefinitely without returning it. He seized the opportunity, cultivated Zhang Peilun and worked through Li Hongzao to secure a decision that both men should return to their substantive posts. But less than a year had passed since his mother’s death, and the Korean disturbance had been quelled. With no further need for force, there was no justification for summoning him from mourning to military service. Fortunately, foreign affairs offered many difficult matters. On the pretext that he was needed to negotiate with the foreign ministers, Li was retained, awaiting a suitable moment for the formal order restoring him. Travelling from his Hefei home to Beijing, he spent many days in Shanghai and gained a strong impression of Zuo’s intention to expel his influence from Liangjiang. Their views on foreign and military affairs also differed sharply. Over the dispute with France in Vietnam, Li believed that “their demands cannot be satisfied, while our military funds cannot bear the strain”. A peaceful settlement was necessary; force must not be used. Zuo, by contrast, advocated supporting Liu Yongfu’s Black Flag Army in helping Vietnam resist France. He supplied arms to Cen Yuying, governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, for onward delivery to Liu, and formally wrote the Zongli Yamen that “the choice between war and peace can be settled in a word”. At present, he argued, “not only do many Western countries consider France in the wrong; they foresee that discord with China must leave the affair without a conclusion and bring irretrievable regret”. France itself feared the great risks of war with China, but, having mounted the tiger, could only bluff. If China wavered, it would fall into the trap. His assessment was that war accorded with justice, suited the circumstances and conformed to opinion both in China and abroad. Because he kept arguing thus, the court specially ordered Li to Guangdong to supervise Vietnamese affairs. This was nominal: Li need not actually go there, since he could negotiate peace with the French minister Bourée in Shanghai or Tianjin. But if Zuo continued urging armed intervention, Li might eventually have to command a war against France from Guangdong—a prospect that threatened to ruin him. The Zongli Yamen was cautious and would not readily accept Zuo’s argument from “justice”. Nevertheless, his advocacy made Li’s negotiations with Bourée more difficult.

zh: 对法如此，对英亦常使李鸿章伤脑筋。英商的海洋电报线希望由吴淞接一条旱线到上海，左宗棠坚持不许；英商希望减轻茧捐，左宗棠亦表反对。而最使李鸿章为难的是，左宗棠倡议洋药土烟加厘一事。『洋药土烟』皆指鸦片，『加厘』便是加『通行税』。左宗棠认为鸦片流毒无穷，主张寓禁于征，奉旨允准后，会同李鸿章与英国公使威妥玛交涉。威妥玛提出洋药进口增加税，行销内地在各关卡所征厘捐不增加；左宗棠也同意了，但每箱的进口税，中国要一百五十两；英国只愿缴八十两。相差太巨，一直没有成议。以后左宗棠外放，交涉由李鸿章接办，而威妥玛奉调回国，希望此一交涉能如英国的条件谈成功，增添他回国以后的面子，李鸿章有心帮忙，却以左宗棠的不肯妥协，以江督的地位表示反对，搞得事成僵局。
en: Britain, too, gave Li headaches. British merchants wanted to connect their submarine telegraph cable at Wusong to Shanghai by a land line; Zuo firmly refused. They sought a reduction in the cocoon levy; he opposed that as well. Most troublesome was his proposal to raise the likin on imported opium and native-grown opium. He regarded opium’s harm as limitless and proposed using taxation as a means of suppression. After imperial approval, he and Li negotiated with the British minister, Thomas Wade. Wade proposed increasing the import duty while leaving inland transit levies unchanged. Zuo agreed in principle, but China demanded a hundred and fifty taels per chest and Britain offered only eighty. The gap was too wide for agreement. After Zuo took a provincial appointment, Li continued the negotiations. Wade, recalled to Britain, hoped to conclude the matter on British terms and return home with enhanced standing. Li wished to help, but Zuo refused to compromise and opposed the terms as governor-general of Liangjiang, producing a deadlock.

zh: 但在事业上最大的冲突是，李鸿章原主『海防』，而张佩纶有个专设『水师衙门』创办新式海军之议，大为李鸿章所欣赏。但左宗棠一到两江，巡阅过海口及长江以后，改变了他原来『陆防』的主张，特意将水师出身的彭玉麟请了来，商量造新式兵舰，而且已经开始在办了。左宗棠首创福建船政，对此道不能说他是外行；因此可以预见的是，将来创办新式海军，左宗棠决不容北洋单独掌权。『海防』、『陆防』之争，只要打倒了他的理论，便无他虑；如今左宗棠亦主张海防，那就变成彼此竞争着办一件事，权不能独专、事不能由心，是李鸿章最不能容忍的一件事。因此，无论看眼前，算将来，李鸿章认为左宗棠是非拔除不可的眼中钉。这得从剪除左宗棠的羽翼着手。李鸿章手下的谋士，都有这样一种见解；且认为第一个目标，应该是胡雪岩。于是上海道邵友濂便与盛宣怀等人，密密商定了一个打击胡雪岩的办法，在洋债还款这件事上，造成胡雪岩的困窘。
en: Their greatest conflict of policy concerned the navy. Li had originally advocated maritime defence, and greatly admired Zhang Peilun’s proposal for a special Naval Yamen and a modern fleet. But after reaching Liangjiang and inspecting the coast and Yangtze, Zuo changed his earlier preference for land defence. He invited Peng Yulin, whose career had begun in the naval forces, to discuss modern warship construction, and work was already under way. Having founded the Fujian shipbuilding establishment, Zuo could not be dismissed as an amateur. It was therefore foreseeable that he would never permit Beiyang sole authority over the future modern navy. In a dispute between land and sea defence, defeating his argument would have removed the difficulty. Now that he too favoured maritime defence, they would compete to carry out the same enterprise. Li could not tolerate sharing authority or being unable to act as he wished. Whether he considered the present or the future, Zuo was a thorn in his eye that must be removed. The first step was to strip away his support. Li’s advisers agreed, and thought Hu Xueyan should be the first target. Shanghai Circuit Intendant Shao Youlian accordingly made a secret plan with Sheng Xuanhuai and others: they would place Hu in difficulty over repayment of a foreign loan.

zh: 其时胡雪岩经手、尚未清结的借款，还有两笔，一笔是光绪四年八月所借的商款，华洋各计，总计六百五十万两；洋款不借借商款，其中别有衷曲，原来光绪三年，由胡雪岩经手，向汇丰银行借款五百万两，借还均用实银，条件是月息一分二厘五，期限七年，连本带利分十四期拔还。每期六个月，仍由浙、粤、江海、江汉四关出票，按期偿还。此外有个附带条件，即商定此项条件后，如果借方作罢，三个月内关票不到，则胡雪岩罚银十五万两；汇丰如果三个月内不交银，罚款相间。这笔借款由于两江总督沈葆桢的介入，一波三折，拖延甚久。其时西征军事颇为顺手，刘锦棠率军自乌鲁木齐南进，并分兵与陕西提督张曜会功吐鲁番，一举克复，回乱首脑之一的白彦虎仓皇西遁；刘锦棠亦推进至吐鲁番盆地西端的托克逊，回众投降者两万余人。但回部首脑经和硕、焉耆，出铁门关在库尔勒地方，跟俄国军方搭上了线，而西征军却因粮饷困难，无法西进，左宗棠着急得不得了。好不容易在五月里谈成功了这笔洋债，至少望梅止渴，军心先是一振；同时在上海、湖北、陕西的三处粮台，借商款应急，亦比较容易措手了。
en: Two loans handled by Hu remained outstanding. One was merchant funding contracted in the eighth month of the fourth year of Guangxu, with Chinese and foreign portions totalling six and a half million taels. Why had merchant funding been used rather than a foreign loan? There was a story behind it. In Guangxu’s third year, Hu had arranged a five-million-tael loan from HSBC, to be advanced and repaid in actual silver. Interest was one and a quarter per cent a month, with principal and interest repaid in fourteen instalments over seven years. Each instalment fell six months apart. As before, repayment was secured by bills issued by the Zhejiang, Guangdong, Shanghai and Jianghan customs. A supplementary condition stipulated that if the borrower abandoned the transaction after agreement, failing to supply the customs bills within three months, Hu would forfeit a hundred and fifty thousand taels. HSBC would incur the same penalty if it failed to deliver the silver within three months. Intervention by Shen Baozhen, governor-general of Liangjiang, caused repeated complications and long delay. The western campaign was then going well. Liu Jintang had advanced south from Urumqi and sent a force to join Shaanxi provincial commander Zhang Yao in an attack that recovered Turfan at one stroke. Bai Yanhu, one of the Muslim rebel leaders, fled west in haste. Liu reached Toksun at the western end of the Turfan basin, and more than twenty thousand Muslim followers surrendered. But the leadership passed through Hoxud and Karashahr, emerged from Iron Gate Pass and established contact with the Russian military at Korla. Meanwhile, shortages of provisions and pay prevented the expeditionary army from advancing west, to Zuo’s intense anxiety. At last the foreign loan was negotiated in the fifth month. Even the prospect was like imagining plums to quench thirst: army morale revived, and the supply offices in Shanghai, Hubei and Shaanxi found it easier to borrow from merchants for immediate needs.

zh: 哪知在办手续时，起了波折，原来英商汇丰银行贷款，照例要由总理衙门出面，致英国公使一个照会，叙明借款条件等等，由英国公使再转行总税务司及驻上海领事，转知汇丰银行照办。这一来，如果贷款放出去收不回，便可由英国向中国交涉；这通照会实际上是中国政府所出的保证书，所以由汇丰银行拟好稿子，交给胡雪岩，再经左宗棠咨请总理衙门办理，而汇丰的稿子中，说明『息银不得过一分』，然则左宗棠的奏折中，何以说是月息一分二厘五？为此，其中处于关键地位的总税务司赫德，表示这笔借款不能成立。这当然要查。左宗棠根据胡雪岩的答复回奏，说汇丰的息银，只有一分，诚然不错，但付款办法是以先令计算，折付银圆；这种银圆，一向在东南各省通用，称之为『烂番银』，西北向不通用，所以仍旧须借以两为单位的现银。但先令的市价，根据伦敦挂牌，早晚不同；到时候如果汇价上涨，胡雪岩便要吃赔帐，所以接洽德商泰来洋行，『包认先令』，这要承担相当风险，泰来洋行得息二厘五，并不为多。左宗棠表示，此案『首尾本属一贯』，只是前次『未经声叙明析』，又力言胡雪岩『息借洋款，实无别故』。很显然的，这是左宗棠硬顶下来的，朝廷不能不买他的老面子；左宗棠心里却觉得很不是味道，从此对胡雪岩的信用便打了一个折扣，可是却不能不用胡雪岩。
en: Complications arose during the formalities. A loan from the British-owned HSBC ordinarily required the Zongli Yamen to notify the British minister of its terms. The minister then instructed the inspector-general of customs and the Shanghai consul to inform HSBC accordingly. If the loan could not be recovered, Britain could then raise the matter with China. In effect, the note was a Chinese government guarantee. HSBC therefore drafted it and gave it to Hu, who passed it through Zuo with a request that the Zongli Yamen act. Yet the bank’s draft said that interest must not exceed one per cent. Why, then, had Zuo’s memorial specified one and a quarter per cent a month? Robert Hart, the inspector-general of customs whose role was crucial, declared the loan could not proceed. An investigation was inevitable. On the basis of Hu’s explanation, Zuo memorialised that HSBC’s interest was indeed only one per cent. But the loan was reckoned in shillings and paid in silver dollars. Those dollars, commonly called “worn foreign silver”, circulated in the southeastern provinces but not in the northwest. The funds therefore still had to be obtained in actual silver measured in taels. The shilling exchange rate varied with London quotations, even between morning and evening. If it rose at the time of conversion, Hu would suffer a loss. He had therefore arranged with the German Tailai Trading House to guarantee the shilling conversion. This involved substantial risk, for which its additional quarter of a percentage point in interest was not excessive. Zuo insisted that the arrangement had been consistent throughout and merely had not previously been explained clearly. He strongly asserted that Hu had no ulterior motive in borrowing abroad. Plainly, he was taking responsibility and standing firm; the court could hardly refuse to respect his seniority. Inwardly, however, he felt badly about it. His trust in Hu diminished, though he could not do without him.

zh: 胡雪岩当然亦想力盖前愆，于是而有借商款的办法，这年——光绪三年年底，左宗棠写给胡雪岩的复信说∶『今岁饷事，拮据殊常，非枢邸严催协饷，筹部款，大局已不可问。洋款枝节横生，非阁下苦心孤诣，竭力维持，无从说起。』现在年关满饷，仍待洋款头批速到，始够支销，除清还鄂欠外，尚须匀拨陕赈及甘属灾黎，所余洋款，除清还沪局借款外，核计敷至明年夏秋之交而止，此后又不知何以为计？尊意以为兵事可慰，饷事则殊可忧，不得不先一年预为之地，洵切实确凿之论，弟心中所欲奉商者，阁下已代为计之，非设身处地，通盘熟筹，不能道其只字，万里同心，不言而喻。『原来胡雪岩早替左宗棠算过了，年底本应发饷；陕甘两省旱灾要赈济，再还了湖北、上海两处借款，到得明年夏秋之间，便又是青黄不接的时期了。借款筹饷要早一年便须着手。可是洋款已不能借。借洋款是国家的责任，虽说由各省协饷，但灾荒连年，各省情形都不好，欠解西征协饷，无法归还欠款，仍须政府设法，所以根本不能再提洋款。而且左宗棠因为借洋款，要受赫德的气，自己亦不大愿意借洋款，尤其是英商的款子。胡雪岩想到左宗棠说过，『息耗太重，如果是商款，楚弓楚得，倒还罢了。洋人赚了我们重利，还要多方挑剔，实在不甘。』同时又一再表示，『何必海关及各省出票？倒象是各省替陕甘来还债；其实还的还是陕甘应得的协饷。我主持西征，筹饷我有全权；协饷不到，先借款子来接济，这就是所谓调度。商人如果相信陕甘相信我，由陕甘出票就可以了，何必劳动总署？』
en: Hu naturally wished to make amends, and devised the merchant-loan method. At the end of that year, Guangxu’s third, Zuo wrote in reply: “This year our finances have been exceptionally strained. Had the prince at the Grand Council not pressed urgently for provincial assistance and arranged funds from the ministry, the whole undertaking would have been beyond saving. Complications arose at every turn in the foreign loan. Without your painstaking ingenuity and tireless support, nothing could have been done. Even now, the year-end payroll depends on the swift arrival of its first advance. After settling the Hubei debt, we must allocate money for famine relief in Shaanxi and the stricken people of Gansu. Of the remaining loan, after repaying the Shanghai office’s borrowings, enough will last only until the turn of summer and autumn next year. What is to be done after that, I do not know. You say that military affairs give comfort but finance gives grave concern, and preparations must begin a year ahead. That is a thoroughly practical and sound judgement. What I wished to discuss, you have already considered for me. Without putting yourself in my position and examining the whole situation, you could not have said a word of it. Across ten thousand li, we are of one mind without needing explanation.” Hu had indeed calculated it all: the year-end payroll, famine relief after drought in Shaanxi and Gansu, and repayment of the Hubei and Shanghai loans would leave another gap around the following summer and autumn. Borrowing for military finance required a year’s preparation. Yet another foreign loan was out of the question. Such loans were national obligations. Though the provinces were to provide the funds, successive disasters had impoverished them, and arrears in their contributions to the western campaign meant that the government would still have to find repayment. Further foreign borrowing could not even be proposed. Moreover, Zuo resented being subjected to Hart’s obstruction and was reluctant to borrow abroad, particularly from British firms. Hu recalled his words: “The interest and charges are too heavy. With merchant money, what Chu loses Chu gains, and that might be tolerable. But foreigners make great profits from us and still find fault at every turn. It is galling.” He had also said repeatedly, “Why must the customs and provinces issue bills, as though they were repaying Shaanxi and Gansu’s debts? The repayments come from contributions those provinces are already owed. I command the western campaign and have full authority to arrange its funds. Borrowing when assistance is late is simply managing cash flow. If merchants trust Shaanxi and Gansu and trust me, bills from those provinces should suffice. Why trouble the Zongli Yamen?”

zh: 因此他设计了一套借商款的办法，往返磋商定议，由胡雪岩邀集商股一百七十五万两；另由汇丰『认股』一百七十五万两，合并三百五十万，组识一个乾泰公司负责借出。照左宗棠的计算，在七年之中，陕甘可得协饷一千八百十万以上，除还洋款以外，至少尚有千万之多，所以借几百万商款，一定能够清偿；但协饷收到的日期不一，多寡不定，所以提出来一个『机圆法话』的要求，第一，不出关票；第二，不定年限，可以早还，亦可以迟还；第三，有钱还钱、无钱暂欠，利息照算，不必定为几个月一期。这是他一厢情愿的想法，胡雪岩只能替他办到不出关票，此外年限定为六年，期次仍是半年一期，利息是一分二。当然借商款亦须奏准；左宗棠于光绪四年八月十六日出奏，一个月以后奉到廷寄∶『借用商款，息银既重，各省关每年除划还本息外，京协各饷，更属无从筹措，本系万不得已之计。此次故念左宗棠筹办各务，事在垂成，准照所议办理。嗣后无论何项急需，不得动辄息借商款，致贻后累。『所谓』京饷『，即是在京的各项开支，包括文武百官的俸给、八旗士兵的饷项，以及一年三次送入宫内供两宫太后及皇帝私人开支的』交进银『在内，是最重要的一笔预算，由于左宗棠动辄借款之累，连京饷都』无从筹措『，这话说得很重了。
en: Hu therefore devised a merchant-loan scheme. After repeated discussion, he undertook to assemble one million seven hundred and fifty thousand taels in merchant subscriptions, with HSBC “subscribing” the same amount. The combined three and a half million would be lent through a company called Qiantai. Zuo calculated that over seven years Shaanxi and Gansu would receive more than eighteen million one hundred thousand taels in provincial assistance. Even after repaying the foreign loan, at least ten million would remain, so a merchant loan of several million could certainly be discharged. But remittances arrived at uncertain times and in varying amounts. He therefore requested flexible terms: first, no customs bills; second, no fixed maturity, so that repayment could be early or late; third, pay when money was available and owe it temporarily when it was not, with interest continuing but no fixed interval between instalments. This was wishful thinking. Hu could secure only the absence of customs bills. The term was fixed at six years, instalments remained half-yearly, and interest was one and a fifth per cent a month. Merchant borrowing also required imperial approval. Zuo memorialised on the sixteenth day of the eighth month of Guangxu’s fourth year. A month later he received the court’s reply: “Merchant loans carry heavy interest. After annual allocations from the provincial and customs revenues for principal and interest, funds for the capital and other military requirements cannot be raised. Such borrowing is a last resort. In consideration of Zuo Zongtang’s undertakings, now approaching completion, the present proposal is approved. Hereafter, whatever the urgency, merchant loans at interest must not be resorted to lightly, imposing burdens on the future.” “Capital funds” covered the expenses of government in Beijing: civil and military salaries, pay for the Eight Banner soldiers, and the silver delivered to the palace three times a year for the private expenses of the two empress dowagers and emperor. It was the most important budget item. To say that even these funds could not be raised because of Zuo’s repeated borrowing was a severe rebuke.

zh: 为此，一直到上年左宗棠奉召入京，为了替刘锦棠筹划西征善后，才迫不得已，在近乎独断独行的情况下，借了汇丰银行招股所贷的四百万两。这两笔款子的风险，都在胡雪岩一个人身上。三百五十万的商款，自光绪五年起分期拔还，几乎已还了一半；而且每期本息约十来万银子，邵友濂亦知道，难不倒胡雪岩，要刁难他，只有在光绪七年所借的那一笔上。这笔款子实收于光绪七年四月，年息九厘九毫五，前两年只付息，不还本，第三年起每年拔本一百万两，分两期给付；光绪九年四月付第一期、十月付第二期，每期各五十万两。以前各次洋债，虽由胡雪岩经手，但如何偿还，不用他来操心，因为各省督抚加了印的『关票』，汇集于江海关后，税务司还要签押负连带责任，如果各省的『关票』不能兑现，税务司可以截留税款，代为抵付。可是这最后一次的四百万两，在借款时为了替刘锦棠解除后顾之忧，左宗棠近乎独断独行，只以为未来数年协饷尚多，不愁无法偿还，所以大包大揽地说∶本银『如期由上海转运局经手交还；如上海无银，应准其向户部如期兑取。』这一惟恐总理衙门及李鸿章策动棘德阴挠，但求成功不惜迁就的承诺，无形之中便将全部风险都加了在胡雪岩的肩头上，因为各省如果不解，汇丰银行一定找胡雪岩，他们不必多费周折，请英国公使出面跟户部打交道；以胡雪岩的财力、信用与担当，每期五十万两银子的本银，亦一定挑得起来。
en: Not until the previous year, when Zuo was summoned to Beijing, had he borrowed again. Obliged to arrange finance for Liu Jintang’s settlement of the western regions, he acted almost on his own authority and took a four-million-tael loan raised by HSBC through subscriptions. The risks on both loans rested entirely on Hu. Repayment of the three-and-a-half-million merchant loan had begun in Guangxu’s fifth year, and nearly half had been paid. Each instalment of principal and interest came to only a hundred thousand taels or so. Shao knew that would not trouble Hu; to obstruct him, he must use the loan contracted in the seventh year. Those funds were actually received in the fourth month of that year, at an annual rate stated as “nine li, nine hao and five”. For the first two years only interest was payable. From the third year, a million taels of principal fell due annually, in two instalments: the first in the fourth month of Guangxu’s ninth year and the second in the tenth, five hundred thousand taels each. Hu had handled earlier foreign loans without having to worry about repayment. The customs bills bore the provincial chiefs’ seals and, once collected at Shanghai Customs, were countersigned by the commissioner, who assumed joint liability. If provincial bills could not be honoured, he could withhold customs revenue to pay them. But with the last four-million-tael loan, Zuo had acted almost independently to free Liu Jintang of financial anxiety. Assuming that future provincial remittances would easily cover it, he had broadly promised that principal would “be repaid on schedule through the Shanghai Transport Office; if Shanghai has no funds, the lender shall be permitted to obtain payment on schedule from the Ministry of Revenue”. He feared that the Zongli Yamen and Li might prompt Hart to obstruct the loan, and accepted concessions to secure it. The promise quietly placed the entire risk on Hu’s shoulders. If the provinces failed to remit, HSBC would certainly approach him. There was no need for the trouble of asking the British minister to negotiate with Revenue. With his resources, credit and willingness to shoulder responsibility, Hu would surely meet each five-hundred-thousand-tael principal instalment.

zh: 话虽如此，五十万两银子到底不是一个小数目。邵友濂与盛宣怀秘密商定，到时候，『挤他一挤』，虽未必能挤倒，至少可以打击打击他的信用。其时——光绪九年春天，中法的关系复又恶化了。本来前一年十一月间，李鸿章与法国公使在上海谈判，已经达成了和平解决在越南的纠纷的三点协议。但法国海军部及殖民部，分别向他们的外交部表示，不满宝海与李鸿章的协议，海军方面且已增兵越南北部的海防。而又恰好法国发生政潮，新内阁的外交部长沙美拉库支持军部的主张，推翻前议，而且将宝海撤任，另派特使德理固专程来华谈判。妙的是法国公使宝海，特为自上海到天津去看李鸿章，他劝李鸿章坚持前议，不防指责法国政府违约；有了这种反对他们政府的法国公使，李鸿章觉得谈和又有把握了，所以仍旧照原定计划，奏请准予给假回籍葬亲。李还不肯回任，但为了开始建设旅顺军港，北洋大臣的差使是接下来了，既然请假，北洋大臣自然由张树声暂署。
en: Even so, half a million taels was no small sum. Shao Youlian and Sheng Xuanhuai secretly agreed to “give him a squeeze” when the time came. They might not bring him down, but could at least damage his credit. That spring, Guangxu’s ninth year, relations with France deteriorated again. In the eleventh month of the previous year, Li and the French minister had reached a three-point agreement in Shanghai for a peaceful settlement of the Vietnamese dispute. But the French naval and colonial authorities separately told their foreign ministry that they objected to Bourée’s agreement. The navy had already sent reinforcements to Haiphong in northern Vietnam. A political change in France then brought a new cabinet. Its foreign minister, Challemel-Lacour, supported the military position, repudiated the agreement, recalled Bourée and sent Tricou as special envoy to negotiate in China. Curiously, Bourée himself travelled from Shanghai to Tianjin to see Li and urged him to uphold their earlier agreement, even accusing the French government of breaking its word. With a French minister opposing his own government, Li felt confident of peace once more. He therefore followed his original plan and requested leave to return home for his mother’s burial. He was still unwilling to resume his former office, but had accepted the Beiyang commission in order to begin construction of the naval harbour at Lüshun. During his leave, Zhang Shusheng would naturally act in that capacity.

zh: 但就在二月里李鸿章在合肥原籍时，法军在越南复又动武，不但攻占越南南定，而且直接侵犯中国在越南权益，招商局运米的船，在海防为法军扣押；设在海防及顺安的两处仓库，为法军占领，其中的存粮及其他物品，当然也被没收了。加以越南政府除行文礼部乞援外，并特派『刑部尚书』范慎来华，效『申包胥哭秦庭』，因此，朝中震动，清议昂扬，都主张采取强硬的对策；甚至驻英兼驻法公使一等毅勇侯曾纪泽，亦打电报回来，建议派军援越，不可对法国让步。当时疆臣亦多主战，云贵总督岑毓英，备战已有多时，但署理两广总督的曾国荃，却不愿轻启战端，清议深为不满，因而主持总署的恭王，一面循外交途径向法国抗议；一面奏准命李鸿章迅回直隶总督本任，接着降谕，派李鸿章以直隶总督的身分迅往广东督办越南事宜，所有广东、广西、云南防军，均归节制。同时命左宗棠筹划江南防军待命南调援越。这时胡雪岩恰好在江宁，便跟左宗棠说∶『好象应该还有张制军回两广本任的上谕；不然，李合肥一到天津，不就是有了两位直隶总署？』『妙就妙在没有张振轩回本任的上谕。』左宗棠答说，『总署也知道李少荃决不会到广东，恐怕也不会回天津。』『这，大人倒多指点指点，让我们也开开茅塞。』『李少荃看在曾文正分上，对曾老九一向是很客气的。当年江宁之围，师老无功，李少荃已经克复了常州，朝命赴援江宁，他按兵不动，为的是不愿分曾老九的功。你想，如今他如果一到广东，曾老九怎么办？』『是，是。』胡雪岩想了一下说∶『大人说李合肥也不会到天津，是怕一到了，张制军就得回广东，那一来不是又要把曾九帅挤走的吗？』『正是如此。』
en: But in the second month, while Li was at his ancestral home in Hefei, French forces resumed hostilities in Vietnam. They not only captured Nam Dinh but directly infringed Chinese interests. A China Merchants ship carrying rice was detained at Haiphong, and its warehouses at Haiphong and Thuan An were occupied; the grain and other property within them were confiscated. Besides formally seeking aid through the Ministry of Rites, the Vietnamese government specially sent its “Minister of Punishments”, Fan Shen, to China, emulating Shen Baoxu’s weeping appeal at the court of Qin. The court was shaken. Moral criticism rose, and all called for a firm response. Even Zeng Jize, the first-rank Marquis Yiyong and minister to Britain and France, telegraphed to urge military aid to Vietnam and no concessions to France. Many provincial chiefs also favoured war. Cen Yuying had long prepared for it, but Zeng Guoquan, acting governor-general of Liangguang, would not lightly begin hostilities, to the critics’ great displeasure. Prince Gong, directing the Zongli Yamen, protested diplomatically to France while obtaining approval to order Li back at once to his substantive post as governor-general of Zhili. Another decree then sent him, in that capacity, urgently to Guangdong to supervise Vietnamese affairs, placing the defence forces of Guangdong, Guangxi and Yunnan under his command. Zuo was simultaneously ordered to prepare troops in the lower Yangtze region for possible dispatch south. Hu happened to be in Jiangning and said to him, “There ought also to be a decree returning Governor-General Zhang to his substantive post in Liangguang. Otherwise, when Li reaches Tianjin, will there not be two governors-general of Zhili?” “The interesting point is precisely that no decree sends Zhang Zhenxuan back,” Zuo replied. “The Zongli Yamen knows Li will never go to Guangdong, and probably will not return to Tianjin either.” “Please enlighten us, Your Excellency.” “Out of respect for the late Lord Wenzheng Zeng, Li has always treated Zeng the Ninth very considerately. During the siege of Jiangning, Zeng’s weary army had made no progress. Li had already recovered Changzhou and was ordered to help, but kept his troops where they were rather than share Zeng’s glory. Think: if he goes to Guangdong now, what is to become of Zeng?” “Yes, yes.” Hu considered it. “And you say he will not go to Tianjin because his arrival would send Zhang back to Guangdong, again displacing Marshal Zeng?” “Exactly.”

zh: 『照此说来，京里只说叫李某某回任，对于张曾两位没不交代，意思也就是要李合能只领虚衔，暂时不必回任。』『不错，举一反三，你明白了。』『那末，李合肥怎么办呢？』左宗棠沉吟了好了一会「问说∶『你看呢？』『我看，他仍旧会到上海。』左宗棠点点头，『我想他也只能先驻上海。』他说∶『而且他也不能忘情上海。』胡雪岩当即说道∶『我本来想跟大人辞了行，回杭州，以后再到上海；照现在看，似乎应该直接到上海的好。』原来各省关应解陕甘，以便还本的协款，都交由江海关代转；所以各省解缴的情况如何，非要胡雪岩到上海去查了才知道。『好，你到上海首先办这件事，看情形如何赶紧写信来。看哪里还没有解到，好及早去催。』胡雪岩的估计很正确，李鸿章果然奏请暂驻上海，统筹全局，察酌南北军情，再取进止。意思是江南防军如果力量不足，无法南调，那就不一定用武，以求和为宜。恭王懂他的用意，奏请准如所请；于是李鸿章在三月底专轮到了上海，驻节天后宫行辕。
en: “Then the capital’s order restoring Li, with no instructions about Zhang or Zeng, means he is to hold the title for the moment without actually resuming the post.” “Correct. You can infer the rest from one point. You understand.” “What will he do, then?” Zuo pondered for a long time. “What do you think?” “I think he will still come to Shanghai.” Zuo nodded. “I too think he can only stay in Shanghai first. Besides, he cannot quite relinquish it.” Hu answered at once, “I had intended to take leave of Your Excellency, return to Hangzhou and go to Shanghai afterwards. In these circumstances, it seems better to go straight to Shanghai.” The provincial and customs contributions assigned to Shaanxi and Gansu for repayment of principal all passed through Shanghai Customs. Only by going there could Hu discover what had actually been remitted. “Good. Make that your first business in Shanghai and write at once with the position. We must know which remittances are missing so that we can press for them early.” Hu’s estimate proved correct. Li petitioned to remain temporarily in Shanghai, coordinating affairs, assessing the military situation in north and south, and deciding his next move accordingly. His meaning was that if the lower Yangtze forces could not spare troops for the south, war need not follow; peace would be preferable. Prince Gong understood and obtained approval. At the end of the third month, Li arrived in Shanghai by a specially arranged steamer and established headquarters at Tianhou Temple.
